title: Embeddings Deep Dive
description: Understand vector spaces, semantic similarity, and how embeddings power search, RAG, and recommendations.

data.text: An embedding is a dense vector of numbers that represents the meaning of a piece of text, image, or other data. Instead of storing words as dictionary indices, embedding models compress them into points in a high-dimensional space where similar meanings cluster together. This mathematical trick is what makes semantic search, RAG, and recommendation systems possible.

Imagine mapping every word in the English language onto a giant 3D globe. Words with similar meanings end up near each other: 'king' and 'queen' are close; 'happy' and 'joyful' are close; 'car' and 'automobile' are close. Embeddings do the same thing, but in 768, 1024, or even 3072 dimensions — spaces too complex for humans to visualize, but perfect for computers.

data.text: Embeddings are learned by a neural network during training. The model reads millions or billions of text examples and adjusts its internal vectors so that words appearing in similar contexts end up with similar vectors. This is a form of unsupervised learning — the model discovers meaning from co-occurrence patterns, not from explicit labels.

data.title: Common embedding models and their dimensions:
Larger isn't always better
data.text: Higher-dimensional embeddings capture more nuance but are slower to compute and search. For many practical applications, 384–768 dimensions offers the best speed/accuracy trade-off. OpenAI's 'small' model (1536 dims) often outperforms larger models on retrieval tasks.

Once text is converted to embeddings, you need a way to measure how similar two vectors are. The three most common metrics are cosine similarity, Euclidean distance, and dot product. Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors (ignoring magnitude), making it the most popular for text embeddings.

Storing and searching millions of embeddings efficiently requires specialized databases. Vector databases use approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms like HNSW or IVF to find the most similar vectors in milliseconds, even across billions of entries. Popular options include Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, and pgvector (for PostgreSQL).

data.title: Practical embedding flow
data.content:
Here's how a typical RAG system uses embeddings:

1. You upload 1,000 company documents
2. The system chunks each document into ~500-token passages
3. Each passage is passed through an embedding model (e.g., text-embedding-3-small)
4. The resulting 1,536-dimensional vectors are stored in a vector database
5. When a user asks a question, the question is embedded the same way
6. The system searches the vector DB for the top-5 most similar passages
7. Those passages are injected into the LLM prompt as context

data.text: Modern embedding models can also encode images, audio, and video into the same vector space as text. CLIP from OpenAI learns a shared space where a photo of a dog and the word 'dog' have nearly identical vectors. This enables cross-modal search — you can search your image library with text queries, or find images similar to a given image.

CLIP embeddings are the backbone of many AI image search tools. Because images and text share the same space, you can query 'a person skiing on a mountain' and get back exactly the right photos — no manual tagging required.

data.title: What embeddings struggle with:
items: Negation — 'not good' and 'good' may have high cosine similarity
Domain shift — embeddings trained on web text perform poorly on legal or medical text without fine-tuning
Older terms — rare historical terms may have poor representations
Ambiguity — the word 'bank' gets a single vector even though it has multiple meanings
Numerical reasoning — '42' and 'forty-two' may have similar vectors but different implications in financial contexts

terms.definition: A mathematical space where each data point is represented as a vector of numbers. Similar items cluster together.
A metric that measures the cosine of the angle between two vectors. Values close to 1 mean very similar; close to 0 means unrelated.
A database optimized for storing and searching high-dimensional vectors using approximate nearest neighbor algorithms.
OpenAI's contrastive model that learns a shared embedding space for images and text.

data.title: Summary
points: Embeddings compress meaning into dense numeric vectors
Similar meanings cluster together in embedding space
Cosine similarity is the most common metric for text similarity
Vector databases enable fast search across millions of embeddings
CLIP-style models create shared spaces for images and text
Embeddings struggle with negation, domain shift, and ambiguity
data.takeaway: Embeddings turn human language into math, enabling computers to understand and compare meaning at scale.
